chunks: To those who say: 'God has ordained that we should not believe an apostle who does not bring burnt offerings,' say: 'Many an apostle had come to you before me with manifest proofs, even with what you mention; then why did you kill them if you were men of truth?'
ai.seo_question: Why did the Jews reject prophets according to the claim in Surah Al-Imran verse 183?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the Banu al-Nadir, who cited the story of Elijah’s sacrifice (1 Kings 18) to demand a similar sign from Prophet Muhammad (PBUH). The Quran refutes this by pointing out their historical inconsistency: if they truly believed in previous prophets, they would not have killed them despite the clear proofs (bayyināt) they brought. This highlights the Shia scholarly view that the demand for miraculous signs often stems from stubbornness rather than genuine seeking of truth.
